_meta.about: Committed source of truth for the Athena Inbox tenancy registry — which projects this machine expects to have a registry entry for, and what each entry says. The live entries are untracked machine-local files at $ATHENA_INBOX_ROOT/projects/<file> (0600, in a 0700 directory); `scripts/setup-inbox-registry --install` materialises them from here by MERGING (it touches only the files declared here and never the rest of the directory), and `ai/bin/check-inbox-registry` fails naming each entry that is missing or drifted. Without these three artifacts a clobbered entry is silent by contract — zero channels, exit 0 — and unrecoverable from git, the 2026-09-17 hook-clobber class. See ai/contracts/athena-inbox.md -> Provisioning, Tenancy: the registry. NO SECRET EVER GOES IN THIS FILE: the machine token lives at ~/.config/athena-inbox-client/config.json and nowhere else. `repo` is the realpath of the project's git common dir and MAY be written with a leading ~/ , which is expanded (and realpath'd, when the path exists) at install and check time.
_meta.stale_after_s: DND-316: per-channel staleness thresholds, set from MEASURED delivery gaps (client log, 2026-09-22/23): slack and flaky each went up to ~5.6h between deliveries while healthy, so the 1800s code default would print STALE most of the day and train every reader to ignore it. 21600 (6h) sits above the measured maximum. agent-messages is on-demand (zero deliveries measured), so 0 disables it. Staleness cannot tell quiet from dark by itself; the relay checks that can (inbox-doctor client-liveness, server-reachability, and the supervisor watchdog) do not depend on these values. Re-measure before lowering.
_meta.harness_alerts: DND-334: ONE maildir conversation, declared from BOTH sides in the custom entry (the contract's mirrored read/write model), because both parties run from this repo: `harness-alerts` is the harness session's side (identity custom, reads to-custom) and `harness-alerts-detector` is the supervisor watchdog's side (identity inbox-client-detector, writes to-custom; it sends through send-mail, which resolves a channel only from the registry entry of its cwd's repo). The harness session reads `harness-alerts` and never sends on either; the detector only sends. DND-692: the shipwright runner (scripts/athena-shipwright-run.sh) is a second sender on `harness-alerts-detector`, under the same identity, for its one-per-signature stale-dirt report; send-mail's .sender.lock serialises the two (contract -> Writer obligations). harness-alerts is declared FIRST so a delivery's shared to-custom doorbell is attributed to it by inbox-wait's rang-channels.
_meta.obligation_1a: walt_ui's `flaky` log channel is declared with producer:"platform" in this same change as one unit with the reader ingestion + DESCRIPTOR_LOG_PRODUCERS admission, per DND-260 obligation-1a. Declaring a platform channel before the reader exists is a silent-loss trap (logchan_scan consumes complete-but-unreadable lines past its offset and the new>0 count gate hides a platform-only channel), so the declaration and the reader are inseparable and ship together — this is intended scope, not scope-creep.
_meta.agent_mail_pair: The custom <-> walt_ui agent-mail maildir pair (custom `walt_ui-mail` / walt_ui `custom-mail`, namespace agent-mail/walt_ui) was added by a shipwright on 2026-09-22 (6e210ba) as the two sessions' local coordination channel. Its fate (epic D20, DND-314 / HG-19): it is KEPT as the same-machine / offline fallback beside the routed `session` inboxes, not retired -- it is the only send path that works with the server down, the client wedged or the machine offline. send-mail's no-flag default sends a maildir-addressed message on it; --routed never falls back to it. See athena:inbox -> Two send paths.
_meta.session: DND-312 (HG-17), epic D41: each project that receives routed session messages declares ONE `log` channel named "session", path "<project>-session.jsonl", producer "platform", and NO `dedupe` (D25: a session message is not a state-change line, carries no authority, and its event_id/delivery_id are references, never dedupe keys; the validator refuses dedupe on a platform channel anyway). The name is `-session`, not `-mail`, because custom already has a MAILDIR channel named "walt_ui-mail" and walt_ui's routed inbox would otherwise have printed as the same name (D41). stale_after_s is 0 for the same reason agent-messages' is: session mail is on-demand, so any threshold would print STALE through ordinary quiet and train readers to ignore it; the last-delivery age is still printed. The channel is per PROJECT, not per session: every worktree of the project resolves it, and two concurrent sessions of one project share it -- the designated-consumer lock decides which one reads. This one list is installed on every machine (desktop and laptop alike); the matching server-side AgentInstances per machine are HG-18's.
_meta.slack_custom: DND-450 (DND-488): custom's `slack` log channel receives ONLY thread-claimed replies -- replies to a Slack thread a custom session started and claimed (ai/contracts/athena-events.md -> Thread replies route to the thread's claimant). Everything else Slack sends still follows the channel route (walt_ui's `slack` channel today). On-demand, so stale_after_s is 0 for the same reason as `session`: any threshold would print STALE through ordinary quiet; never_delivered until the first claimed reply is the expected state, not a fault. dedupe and schema_v match walt_ui's slack channel, because the producer is the same Slack encoder. The matching server-side AgentInstance (inbox_name custom-slack.jsonl) is required on every machine that runs custom sessions, or the server refuses the claim and the delivery (both-ends-or-dark).
